experiment: B3.3 paired resume A/B (FULL vs RETIRED context) via `claude -p --resume`, claude-sonnet-5
method: Truncate a real A_native Step-7 session at cut turn t*, reconstruct the worktree state by replaying edits<=t*, stub the tool-result content of every B3-retired object (superseded within-prefix, or safe tail at tail_turn+5) in the RETIRED arm only, resume BOTH arms with the same continuation prompt (budget-capped), and compare the downstream trajectory. No API key available (SDK blocked); the only live path was the OAuth `claude` CLI, so retirement was applied by hand-editing the resumable transcript.
caveats: n=3 tasks, 1 cut point each, 1 rep per arm (tiny)
no docker/linux, so no SWE-bench pass/fail grading: 'same fix' means the RETIRED arm edited the SAME source files as the FULL arm (and as the native run), not a verified test pass
retirement is MECHANICAL (superseded + tail>=tail_turn+5), not the B3.1 safety-filtered set -- so if anything this OVER-retires
worktree state reconstructed via edit-replay (old_string match can drift); both arms share the same reconstructed state
model is non-deterministic and only 1 rep/arm was run

tasks.note: cut landed AFTER the fix was already complete (edits start turn 8); no continuation work for either arm

summary.finding: Retirement never broke the task: in all 3 tasks the RETIRED arm reached the SAME fix (same source files edited) as the FULL arm. Retired-object re-reads were near-identical between arms because the only re-reads are of the edit-TARGET file, which agents re-read right before editing REGARDLESS of whether an earlier read is resident -- so retiring that earlier read costs ~nothing. Non-target retired objects (query.py, compiler.py, tests.py, timezone.py, bash outputs, etc.) were NEVER re-read.
summary.implication: The live signal is consistent with B3.1's mechanical 95-99% safety, and slightly stronger: even edit-target reads (which B3.1's D0/D1 flags as 'unsafe') cost ~nothing to retire, because the agent re-reads them for the Edit anyway.
